passage:
A historical photo showed workers building a road. The caption said the project had brought progress to the region.
In class, students looked more carefully. The photo also showed tired faces and simple tools. They asked who benefited from the road and who paid the cost.
The teacher said photos can support different stories depending on the caption.
Students wrote two captions for the same photo: one from a government view and one from a worker's view.
The exercise taught them that images are evidence, but not complete truth.
A photograph freezes one moment. Interpretation decides what that moment is used to say.
